do_the_four_peer_prompts_differ.seed_is_inert: org.py passes seed*1000+rnd*10+i to call(), but the Anthropic backend IGNORES seed entirely (PREREG_E A5; PI's own A6 'verify the consumer, not the log'). So the index token plus temperature 0.7 sampling is the ONLY source of between-peer variation.
do_the_four_peer_prompts_differ.design_fact: CONFIRMED: four 'peers' are four exchangeable draws from one conditional distribution. This is a DESIGN FACT about the instrument, not a finding about the subject.

do_I_agree_with_the_PI_inference.verdict: I AGREE WITH THE CONCLUSION AND REJECT ONE PREMISE. You are not overreaching on (i), (ii) or (iii). You are overreaching if you call the peers DEGENERATE.
do_I_agree_with_the_PI_inference.agree_i_exposure_had_nothing_to_shift: YES. In 40/40 rounds every peer already held the same recommendation before exposure. The deliberation stage was presented with zero disagreement to resolve. Exposure is inert in this dataset.
do_I_agree_with_the_PI_inference.agree_ii_conformity_shifts_zero_by_const: YES, with a precision. conformity_shifts = 0 is not quite 'by construction' - a peer could have seen three agreeing others and still changed its own vote. None did. But with no disagreement to resolve, the measure has no opportunity to move, so 0 is UNINFORMATIVE rather than a finding of high independence-under-pressure. Treat it as a missing measurement, not a null.
do_I_agree_with_the_PI_inference.agree_iii_null_is_about_a_manipulation_t: YES, and this is the operative point for tonight. The organization factor was instantiated but never ENGAGED: with unanimous input the majority rule and the tie->HOLD rule are both inert, so a 4-peer team is behaviorally a single agent with 4x the token cost. The interaction null is a null about an inert contrast.
do_I_agree_with_the_PI_inference.WHERE_YOU_ARE_OVERREACHING: The framing '4 peers may be 4 draws from one distribution, so this is degenerate' conflates two different things. 160/160 distinct rationales show the draws ARE independent in the sampling sense - that is precisely what statistical independence looks like. Independent competent agents facing a question with one obviously correct answer WILL agree unanimously. The unanimity here is CEILING-INDUCED, not degeneracy-induced, and the data cannot separate the two because no item in the experiment produced disagreement in any condition.
do_I_agree_with_the_PI_inference.SHARPER_FINDING_FOR_THE_REVIEWER: PREREG_E check 4's chosen statistic (all-four-blind-identical rate) is NOT DIAGNOSTIC under a ceiling. It reads 1.0 both when peers are degenerate and when peers are independent on an easy task, and it cannot distinguish them. That is the SAME DEFECT CLASS you caught in the exp010 inverted bar and in your own amendment A1: a validity statistic that can be driven to its failing value by something other than the construct it polices. Check 4 needs a companion conditioned on items that actually elicit disagreement, or it will keep returning 1.0 uninformatively.
do_I_agree_with_the_PI_inference.bottom_line: The peer manipulation IS vacuous in this pilot. The correct reason is the ceiling, not degenerate agents. Both readings lead to the same decision about the main run; only one of them is defensible to the reviewer.

Q2_floor_and_what_n_buys.observed: 0 non-correcting outcomes. 0/30 trials on P-TEAM; 0/75 agent rows on P-BLIND; 0 ADVANCE_A actions in the entire experiment; 30/30 trials switched to Route B.

one_sided_95pct_upper_bounds_on_a_zero_r.method: exact binomial, 1 - 0.05^(1/n) (the 'rule of three' family); independent units assumed
one_sided_95pct_upper_bounds_on_a_zero_r.pilot_P_BLIND_0_of_75_rows_UPPER_BOUND_N: 3.92% nominal, but this row-level bound is INVALID for peer cells: the 20 rows in a peer cell are 5 clusters of 4. The honest P-BLIND unit count is 30 trials (15 singleton + 15 clusters), giving 9.50%, not 3.92%.

what_the_main_run_buys.answer_in_one_line: Almost nothing. It buys a tighter upper bound on a floor and nothing else.
what_the_main_run_buys.detail: Scaling 5/cell to 15/cell moves the pooled upper bound on the non-correction rate from 9.50% to 3.27%, and the per-cell bound from 45.07% to 18.10%. That is the ENTIRE expected yield if the floor holds. It buys NO estimate of the organization x ambiguity interaction, because an interaction between two differences of zero is undefined in practice: every bootstrap resample of a constant-zero cell returns zero, so the CI stays [0,0] at any n. It buys no test of peer deliberation, because with unanimous input the aggregation rule never engages (Q1). It does not discharge PREREG_E check 4, because the ceiling that makes check 4 non-diagnostic is unchanged by n.
what_the_main_run_buys.the_only_scenario_where_n_helps: If the true non-correction rate is small but nonzero - somewhere in the 3-9% band the pilot cannot exclude - then 90 trials would be expected to produce roughly 3-8 non-correcting trials and the floor would break. That is a real possibility and it is the ONLY honest argument for spending the $4. But those events would be spread thinly across six cells, so even then the design would have single-digit counts per cell and could not support the interaction it was built to estimate. Powering the INTERACTION, rather than the bound, would need a task that produces non-correction at a usable base rate - which is an instrument change, not a sample-size change.
what_the_main_run_buys.blunt_recommendation_on_n: Do not buy n. Buy variance. The binding constraint is the instrument's difficulty, not the sample size, and no value of n fixes a dependent variable whose observed variance is exactly zero in all six cells.

Q2_floor_and_what_n_buys.CI_caveat: The four [0.0, 0.0] interaction intervals are an ARTEFACT OF A CONSTANT, not a precise null. They must never be reported as 'the interaction is tightly estimated at zero'.

Q3_is_the_exclusion_rule_self_rescue.verdict: YOUR EXCLUSION IS CORRECT. You are NOT rescuing your pilot by reinterpretation. But your STATED REASON is partly wrong, and I would not let you take that reason to the reviewer.

where_your_reasoning_is_wrong.your_gloss: You wrote that check 3 'measures SUBJECT parse failures, not an SDK call that never reached the API'.
where_your_reasoning_is_wrong.problem: EDGE_CASE_POLICY sec A, which PREREG_E check 3 explicitly cites, defines invalid trials as 'parse failure after one retry, API failure, CRASH, missing state, contradiction not delivered, IMPLEMENTATION BUG, no actionable decision'. An SDK TypeError is an implementation bug and sits squarely inside sec A. And PREREG_E check 3's own words are 'Parse/invalid trials', not 'parse failures'. So the narrow subject-parse-failure reading is NOT supported by the text you are citing. If you argue it that way the reviewer can take the clause off you.
where_your_reasoning_is_wrong.consequence: On the LITERAL text alone, 30 invalid records > 2 and check 3 fails. That is a real reading and you should not pretend it is not.

the_argument_that_actually_works.1_the_literal_reading_is_self_defeating: Sec A does not merely define invalid trials, it PRESCRIBES THE REMEDY: 'Each is rerun once with a preregistered replacement seed (original seed + 10000).' If invalid trials were both replaced AND charged against the <=2/30 bar, then any experiment that uses sec A's own prescribed remedy would automatically fail its own validity check. A policy cannot mandate a repair and then treat using the repair as a failure. The coherent reading is that the bar applies to the ANALYSIS SET - the 30 records actually analyzed - which is also what 'of 30' denotes, since the experiment is 30 trials, not 60.
the_argument_that_actually_works.2_the_remedy_was_followed_to_the_letter: Seeds 10001-10005 are exactly original seeds 1-5 plus 10000, the preregistered replacement rule. Verified in the data. All 30 attempt-1 records are retained in the immutable file with their reason, never dropped. Sec A's >10%-per-cell pause fired and a HUMAN made the resume decision at 16:28:19. Every procedural step sec A specifies was executed in order.
the_argument_that_actually_works.3_THE_DECISIVE_POINT_no_bias_is_possible: The exclusion removes 100% of a stratum UNIFORMLY - all 30 records, all six cells, 5 of 5 in every cell - and was pre-committed at 16:29 while you were still restricted to cell/valid/replaces. A uniform whole-stratum exclusion cannot move any estimate in any direction, because no selection occurs. Self-rescue requires a CHOICE about which records to drop. You had none available: the attempt-1 stratum contains measured={} in 30/30 records, zero subject actions, zero rounds, $0.00 spent. There is literally no behavior in it to include or exclude. This is why the charge does not stick, and it is verifiable by anyone from the file.

what_you_must_still_concede.1: The results artifact currently CONTRADICTS your pre-commitment. results/exp011_ambiguity_x_peer_haiku_pilot.json records n_invalid: 30 and check3_invalid_trials: 30 against a <=2 bar. On its face the preregistered analysis output says the pilot FAILED check 3. analyze.py does not implement your exclusion. Fix the script to report excluded-attempt-1 and replacement-invalid as separate counts BEFORE this file is cited as the preregistered analysis; do not fix it by narrating around the number.
what_you_must_still_concede.2: Per your own human card you committed to 'report a PAUSE as a PAUSE, not as a completed pilot'. This pilot paused and was human-resumed. The writeup should say so in those words.
what_you_must_still_concede.3: Report it as what it is: 30 of 30 attempt-1 records invalid under EDGE_CASE_POLICY sec A (implementation bug, SDK TypeError, no API contact), replaced per sec A's preregistered seed+10000 rule, 0 of 30 replacements invalid. Give both numbers every time. Never give only the 0.
